name: Coteaux d'Aix-en-Provence

limits: For red and rosé wine, Grenache: at least 20%
For white wine, Vermentino: at least 50%
For white wine, Verdejo, Floreal, Souvignier Gris and Sauvignac together: at most 5%

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Indication Géographique Protégée, the tier below AOC. It replaced vin de pays in 2009.
France's simplest category, in use since 2010. It replaced vin de table.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.

notes: Provence is known mainly for rosé, which is normally dry, with zesty acidity.
Its reds and whites are full bodied with intense aromas, and the dry whites have low acidity and herbal notes.
Many wines carry the scents of the garrigue: wild lavender, rosemary and thyme.
Some Provence wines resemble Southern Rhône wines, sharing grapes and some of their style.

blurb.text: A Provence appellation for red, rosé and white wine. Grenache, Syrah, Mourvèdre, Counoise and Cinsault lead the reds and rosés, and Vermentino the whites.
